icon:: 🗺️

- # Where things are
  - A short map of Tine's main places, so the recipes in this Guide make sense on first read: the page in the middle, the left sidebar, the tab strip, the right sidebar, and Settings and Help. Each place links to the workflow that teaches it — nothing here is a rulebook.
- ## The middle: one route per pane
  - Each pane shows the **page or PDF** its active tab points to. Tine opens on the **journal feed** — one continuous, editable list of days — and the **Journals** item in the left sidebar always takes you back to it.
  - Everything you write is a **block** (one bullet). Blocks nest under other blocks to form the outline, and any block can carry a task, a date, a link, or its own id for references from elsewhere.
  - Press **Ctrl+K** at any time to jump to a page by name or to text inside any block.
  - The reading column has a width cap. Press **t w** to toggle wide mode, which drops the cap; Settings → **Appearance** → **Advanced** holds **Standard page width** and **Wide page width** if you want your own numbers.
  - If one region of the screen — the page, the sidebar, a references section, or the conflict panel — fails to draw, that region shows a small card saying so, with a **Retry** button, instead of leaving the whole window blank. Your files on disk are not touched by it.
- ## The left sidebar: your graph's contents
  - At the very top sits the workspace switcher — saved window layouts, covered in [[tine-guide/Workflows/Keep context visible]]. Just under it, the graph-name menu switches between the graphs Tine knows, with **Open graph…** and **New graph…** beside them — on desktop, Shift-click a graph row to open it in a second window instead of switching this one. Right-click a row for the same thing as a menu item — **Open in a new window** — along with **Open here**, **Show in folder**, **Copy path**, and **Remove from this list**. The row for the graph you already have open shows the two open actions greyed out, so the menu keeps its shape wherever you click.
  - Below the menu: **Journals**, then fold-up **Favorites** and **Recent** (each appears once it has something in it), **All pages**, and the **Namespaces** tree, where `Project/Roadmap` nests under `Project`. Favorites and Recent remember whether you left them open or folded.
  - Every row is a whole-row click target: clicking the blank space to the right of a short page name opens that page, just like clicking the name itself. Shift-click a row for the right sidebar, middle-click for a background tab, right-click for the page menu.
  - Favorites can be arranged without changing what Logseq sees: choose **+ New group**, rename the plain-text label, then drag favorites or groups left/right to lift or nest them to any depth. Deleting a group keeps everything it held one level up. Tine stores that richer arrangement on an ordinary editable page while keeping `config.edn :favorites` as Logseq's flat list; [[tine-guide/Workflows/Find and revisit]] walks the safe path.
  - The **+ New page** button at the bottom opens the same Ctrl+K box; a name that matches nothing becomes a page you can create. When Syncthing, Dropbox or a merge leaves pages that need a decision, an **N conflicts** badge appears beside it — see [[tine-guide/Reference/Files, external edits, and backups]]. Press **t l** to fold the whole sidebar away, and **t l** again to bring it back.
- ## The tab strip: what's open
  - Every open page or PDF keeps a tab along the top, browser-style: click to switch, **Ctrl+W** to close. Middle-click anything that opens a page — a link, a search result, a bullet's dot — to park it in a background tab without leaving this one. PDF links open in a companion pane by default, and their tabs can be dragged between panes like page tabs. Tabs come back after a restart.
  - Tabs are a desktop feature — the mobile app hides the strip so one page or PDF route keeps the screen, with Back returning through its history.
- ## The right sidebar: parked context
  - Anything you want **beside** the current page rather than instead of it — another page, or zoomed into one bullet — goes to the right sidebar: **Shift-click** a link or a bullet's dot. Items there are live editors, not previews. Press **t r** to show or hide the whole sidebar.
- ## Settings and Help
  - The gear at the top right (or press **t s**) opens **Settings**: appearance (Light, System or Dark, interface size, wide mode), editor behavior, journals, files, backups & recovery, the graph, plugins, help & diagnostics, and the remappable **Keyboard shortcuts** list. The search box at the top filters every setting.
  - Settings opens as a small dialog. The button beside its search box makes it fill the window, which is easier to read through; Tine remembers which size you left it at and opens it that way next time.
  - The **?** button at the bottom right (or press **Shift+?**) opens Help: this Guide, the shortcut reference, the features documentation, the bug-report and release-notes links, and the Welcome screen.
- ## On a phone
  - Below a 640 px window width, either sidebar opens as an overlay on top of the current route instead of shrinking it — tap the shaded outside edge, press Esc, or use Android Back to dismiss. Split panes and the tab strip are desktop-only on a phone-sized screen.
  - [[tine-guide/Reference/Platforms and mobile]] separates narrow-window behavior from native-app behavior and maps each platform's shipping surface.
- ## Where next
  - New here? [[tine-guide/Welcome to Tine]] walks the first hands-on minutes. To put these places to work — parking, pinning, splitting, and saving the layout — continue with [[tine-guide/Workflows/Keep context visible]]; [[tine-guide/Features/Tips & shortcuts]] is the compact shortcut map.
